location: PDF p14, Appendix G, Equations (18)–(19) and concluding paragraph
original_statement_summary: The second-order term (h_v/2)*(m′)^2 in the Taylor approximation is said not to cancel across components of the m-th order alternating interaction sum, and this is used to conclude the interaction effect increases with order.
problem: For exact second-degree polynomials, the m-th finite difference vanishes for every m>2. Thus the displayed quadratic approximation alone cannot establish the asserted higher-order growth.
counterexample_or_derivation: For m=3 and v_t=t², the alternating binomial sum is 9−3·4+3·1−0=0. More generally Σ_{t=0}^m (−1)^{m−t} C(m,t) t²=0 for m>2.
impact_scope: Appendix G heuristic saturation/high-order explanation; this observation does not by itself refute the independent AND-OR matching proofs in C/E or the empirical findings.
authorization: No paper statements, corpus, or formalization were changed.
qualification: Finite-difference cancellation applies when v_m′ is the same quadratic polynomial with coefficients independent of subset/order; the Taylor remainder and whether coefficients in Eq18 vary with the subsets must be reviewed before concluding a paper error.
